subject: english-literature

moments.title: Atonement published
moments.body: September 2001: Atonement published. A young girl's false accusation in 1935 destroys a relationship; the novel follows the consequences through WWII (Dunkirk, the war hospitals) and the postwar period. The final section reveals the novel itself is metafiction — the now-elderly Briony's attempt at atonement through narrative.
moments.takeaway: McEwan had been a major novelist since the 1970s. Atonement was his most ambitious and most commercially successful work.

moments.title: Plagiarism controversy
moments.body: 2006: it emerges that Atonement's hospital scenes draw heavily on Lucilla Andrews's memoir 'No Time for Romance' (1977). McEwan acknowledges the source. The controversy briefly raised plagiarism questions before subsiding — McEwan had cited Andrews in afterword.
moments.takeaway: Historical fiction's relationship to source material has been the subject of much subsequent discussion. McEwan's case was a high-profile example.

moments.title: Joe Wright's film
moments.who: Joe Wright, Keira Knightley, James McAvoy
moments.body: 2007: Joe Wright's adaptation. Strong critical reception; six Oscar nominations (one win — best original score). The film's Dunkirk beach tracking shot became a celebrated technical achievement.
moments.takeaway: The film made the novel accessible to a wider audience and intensified its presence in popular culture.

now.title: Contemporary British fiction
now.body: Atonement is one of the most-taught contemporary British novels at A-level and university. Its formal experimentation, its WWII setting, and its metafictional ending all give classrooms much to discuss. McEwan's prose style — precise, lucid, ironic — has shaped a generation of British fiction.
now.open_questions: Does Briony's 'atonement' work? She gives her lovers a happy ending in fiction they were denied in reality. The novel makes us question what fiction can do morally.

reflection: A novel about a child's lie, the cost of false witness, and the limits of fictional atonement has become a touchstone of 21st-century English literature. McEwan's combination of precise prose, deep moral seriousness and formal play makes Atonement one of the most ambitious recent British novels.
